text: Smart surgical instruments and systems with integrated sensor telemetry

metadata.title: Smart surgical instruments and systems with integrated sensor telemetry

text: A surgical instrument system includes an end effector, an articulation joint, a drive assembly, and an electronic control system. The control system continuously monitors telemetry from sensors on the end effector to dynamically regulate tissue clamping pressure and motor current.

metadata.title: Smart surgical instruments and systems with integrated sensor telemetry

text: Claim 1: A surgical instrument comprising: an end effector configured to grasp tissue; a sensor array positioned on the end effector to measure real-time tissue impedance; and a microcontroller configured to modulate motor drive current based on said impedance.

metadata.title: Smart surgical instruments and systems with integrated sensor telemetry

text: Claim 2: The surgical instrument of claim 1, further comprising an articulation joint coupled to the end effector and an electromechanical actuator responsive to the microcontroller.

metadata.title: Smart surgical instruments and systems with integrated sensor telemetry

text:
Background of the Invention
Surgical stapling and cutting devices require precise force management to prevent tissue damage while ensuring secure staple formation. Traditional mechanical linkages lack real-time feedback under variable tissue thickness.

metadata.title: Smart surgical instruments and systems with integrated sensor telemetry

text:
Summary of the Invention
The present invention provides an integrated sensor feedback loop that continuously samples tissue characteristics and dynamically throttles actuator displacement.

metadata.title: Smart surgical instruments and systems with integrated sensor telemetry

text: Generating contextual summaries from multi-source electronic documents

metadata.title: Generating contextual summaries from multi-source electronic documents

text: Methods and systems for generating contextual summaries from electronic documents using entity graph extraction and cross-reference frequency weighting. Candidate summary sentences are scored based on semantic centrality and topical cohesion.

metadata.title: Generating contextual summaries from multi-source electronic documents

text: Claim 1: A method for generating contextual summaries comprising: parsing a plurality of input documents to identify named entities; constructing an entity-relation co-occurrence graph; and ranking sentences according to eigenvector centrality on said graph.

metadata.title: Generating contextual summaries from multi-source electronic documents

text: Claim 2: The method of claim 1, further comprising filtering redundant sentences whose cosine similarity exceeds a predefined threshold.

metadata.title: Generating contextual summaries from multi-source electronic documents

text:
Background
Large text corpora present significant challenge for knowledge workers attempting to distill key insights across disparate technical specifications.

metadata.title: Generating contextual summaries from multi-source electronic documents

text:
Detailed Description
The system creates an entity-centric summary by linking concepts across documents and extracting representative sentence clusters.

metadata.title: Generating contextual summaries from multi-source electronic documents

text: Document chunking and hierarchical indexing for dense semantic retrieval

metadata.title: Document chunking and hierarchical indexing for dense semantic retrieval

text: Hierarchical segmentation and semantic chunking of semi-structured documents for vector similarity search. Text passages are chunked along structural headings and syntactic sentence boundaries to preserve local semantic context.

metadata.title: Document chunking and hierarchical indexing for dense semantic retrieval

text: Claim 1: A computer-implemented system comprising: a structural parser configured to identify heading levels in a document; a chunking engine configured to segment content between heading levels into bounded passages with rolling overlap; and an embedding index storing vector representations of each passage.

metadata.title: Document chunking and hierarchical indexing for dense semantic retrieval

text: Claim 2: The system of claim 1, wherein the bounded passages enforce strict sentence boundary alignment.

metadata.title: Document chunking and hierarchical indexing for dense semantic retrieval

text:
Technical Field
The present disclosure relates generally to information retrieval and document indexing for dense neural representations.

metadata.title: Document chunking and hierarchical indexing for dense semantic retrieval

text:
Detailed Description
Document passages are divided into contiguous chunks that preserve heading context as structural metadata alongside passage text.

metadata.title: Document chunking and hierarchical indexing for dense semantic retrieval

text: Information retrieval using hybrid lexical and dense vector representations

metadata.title: Information retrieval using hybrid lexical and dense vector representations

text: Systems and methods for ranking search candidates using reciprocal rank fusion over sparse lexical inverted indices and dense embedding projections. Combined scoring balances keyword exact matches with semantic intent.

metadata.title: Information retrieval using hybrid lexical and dense vector representations

text: Claim 1: A search system comprising: a lexical retrieval engine producing a first ranked list of document identifiers; a dense vector retrieval engine producing a second ranked list of document identifiers; and a rank fusion engine combining said first and second ranked lists via reciprocal rank fusion.

metadata.title: Information retrieval using hybrid lexical and dense vector representations

text: Claim 2: The search system of claim 1, wherein reciprocal rank fusion assigns scores according to the formula 1/(k + rank).

metadata.title: Information retrieval using hybrid lexical and dense vector representations

text:
Background
Purely lexical search engines miss synonymy and paraphrasing, whereas dense vector models can fail on rare technical alphanumeric codes.

The present invention relates to intellectual property analytics, particularly computerized systems for evaluating patent novelty against existing prior art disclosures.

text: Claim 2: The system of claim 1, wherein entity nodes comprise chemical compounds, mechanical components, and algorithmic processes.

text: Neural re-ranking and cross-encoder scoring for document retrieval

metadata.title: Neural re-ranking and cross-encoder scoring for document retrieval

text: A two-stage information retrieval architecture wherein initial candidates from lexical and embedding retrieval are scored using a cross-attention transformer that jointly processes query and passage tokens.

metadata.title: Neural re-ranking and cross-encoder scoring for document retrieval

text: Claim 1: A method of re-ranking document passages comprising: receiving a set of top-k document candidates from a bi-encoder retrieval index; forming paired query-passage token sequences; and passing each paired sequence through a cross-encoder transformer to compute a relevance probability.

metadata.title: Neural re-ranking and cross-encoder scoring for document retrieval

text: Claim 2: The method of claim 1, wherein the top-k document candidates are selected via approximate nearest neighbor search.

metadata.title: Neural re-ranking and cross-encoder scoring for document retrieval

text:
Detailed Description
Cross-encoder architectures evaluate all-to-all cross attention between query terms and candidate document passages, resolving contextual ambiguity.

metadata.title: Patent classification and prior art identification using deep convolutional networks

text: Multi-label classification of patent disclosures across IPC and CPC hierarchies using character-level and word-level neural representations. Class predictions guide selective prior-art partition filtering.

metadata.title: Patent classification and prior art identification using deep convolutional networks

metadata.title: Patent classification and prior art identification using deep convolutional networks

text: Claim 2: The method of claim 1, wherein the classification model outputs calibrated confidence probabilities for each predicted subclass.

Patent databases contain millions of filings organized into fine-grained classification taxonomies requiring automated categorization.
